fact_bindings.statement: Decoded EVSE voltage/current and Pack voltage/current are dynamic during the capture; reported ranges are 0–365.478578 V, 0–133.0892539 A, 8.17–365.25 V, -219.6–27.8 A, and 347.4–365.3 V for the second Pack-voltage field.
Decoded SOC increased from its reported minimum 27.5 to maximum 31.0, and two charge-energy counters increased over their observed ranges.
The observations are compatible with an actual charging-energy transfer, but sign convention, EVSE-current scaling, simultaneity, and semantic validity prevent a quantitative closure claim.

control_tree_mapping.reason: Both boundaries have dynamic voltage/current candidates and cumulative response, but definitions and synchronized closure are unvalidated.

evidence_requirement_mapping.reason: Actual-side evidence is present, but direct Request is absent and quantitative semantic validity is unresolved.
A charging interval is plausible, but the package does not establish a validated 20–30 s stable window across all semantic layers.

findings.semantic_hypothesis: EVSE-side and Pack-side actual quantities plus rising energy/SOC can form an energy cross-check after their definitions and time-aligned scaling are validated.

alternative_explanations.description: Global ranges combine different times and do not represent one simultaneous operating point.
alternative_explanations.minimum_check: Use a future externally bounded stable interval and compute simultaneous U, I and power on each boundary.

findings.uncertainty: High for quantitative closure; medium for the weaker conclusion that charging-energy-related quantities changed together.

fact_bindings.statement: Decoded enable, charging-status, and fast-charge-contactor fields change back during the late capture interval.
Decoded charger-present/cable/latch fields later return toward their initial reported states.
This is compatible with charging exit followed by connection release, but the stop entry and request withdrawal are not directly observed.
No human stop or unplug time can be assigned from these CAN transitions.

fact_bindings.statement: Decoded thermal request/target and execution candidates are dynamic, including flow, pump target, pump actual and coolant-flow actual.
Decoded thermal-state candidates also change, with reported coolant-inlet range 26.0–59.625 degC and model maximum range 33.5–35.0.
These fields could form a thermal request–execution–temperature companion line, but their early activity and unvalidated semantics prevent attribution specifically to DC charging.
